lesson.menu_desc: Restaurant survival + would like and countable / uncountable -- 27 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- Eating Out
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 3 -- Eating Out
lesson.grammar_point: would like + countable and uncountable nouns

items.situation: You walk in without booking and you want a table for two by the window.
tips: Start with I would like, never with I want.
Say how many people, then where you would like to sit.

items.situation: The server asks how you want the steak and you do not want it well done.
tips: One expression answers the whole question.
Add please at the end and nothing else is needed.

items.situation: You want water for the table and rice with the meat.
tips: One of them is countable and one is not.
Use some for the one you cannot count.

items.situation: Your glass is empty and the drink is included in the price.
tips: There is one word for another glass of the same drink.
Ask with Could I have, not with Bring me.

items.situation: The meal is over, you are in a hurry and you also want to take the rest of the food with you.
tips: Two requests in one turn: the paper and the food.
The food you take away has a two-word name.

listenings.text: Thank you for calling the Copper Kitchen. We are open from twelve to eleven every day. Our kitchen serves appetizers until ten, and the last main course goes out at ten thirty. On Tuesdays every main course comes with a free side dish. We do not add a tip to the check, so please leave what you think is fair. If you would like food to go, press two and we will take your order now.

Good evening and welcome. Let me tell you about tonight before you order. The appetizer of the day is tomato soup, and the main course is grilled salmon with two side dishes. The steak comes medium rare unless you ask for something else. Water and coffee come with a free refill. If you finish and there is still food on the plate, we can pack it to go. I will be back in five minutes to take your order.

extra_audio.text: First, the server shows Thiago to the table and brings the menu. Then he orders some sparkling water and an appetizer. After that, he asks for the steak and says how he would like it cooked. Next, he chooses a side dish and asks for a refill of water. Finally, he asks for the check and leaves a tip.
